title: Float or sink?
card: Drop things into the water tank.

predict.prompt: Which things will float and which will sink? Tap each one to sort your guesses.

try: Tap each thing to drop it into the tank. Watch where it goes!
result: The wood, the ice, the leaf and the dry sponge floated. The stone, the iron nail, the gold ring and the glass marble sank to the bottom.
why: Floating depends on how heavy a thing is for its size. Scientists call this its density. A thing that is lighter than the same amount of water floats; a thing that is heavier sinks.
Most wood, ice and leaves are lighter than water for their size, and a dry sponge is mostly air. Stone, iron, gold and glass are much heavier than water for their size, so they sink.
Shape matters too! A steel ship floats because its hollow hull holds lots of air. Pumice, a stone full of bubbles from a volcano, can float as well.
